The term professionals is not defined in the collective bargaining agreement, so does someone playing on loan under a standard player contract before the entry-level contract kicks in count as a 'Professional'? Right, since nobody has any questions I want to clarify my idea for a forum in a city in the region. Really it's a simple idea. There is an online community for the city where anybody can go to discuss and debate topics relevant to the area. There would be no mechanism for legally binding resolutions initially but with time I could see allowing it. It will be a pure democracy where every participant has a vote in any suggestion made.

There will be one thread per week with discussion. Topics can be submitted before the start of the thread. Each topic will be part of a single comment in the thread for simplicity. So if, for example, an individual submits a topic prior to the thread, then that individual comments with their stance on the topic and all discussion of that topic is limited to replies to that comment. This is really just to keep discussion organized. Any topic not submitted and put on the agenda may be commented on in the thread and added to the agenda, but everybody must still discuss the idea as a response to that first comment.

There will be a forum head, whose job it is to post the thread and run the session. Rules and bylaws for elections will be determined by general consensus in the first session. I will be the first forum head (if elected) and then a new forum head will be elected in no more than 3 weeks from my taking office. This way the forum will be independent before my term is over.

There will be bylaws for proposing and voting on a referendum. These bylaws will all be determined by the forum after it is formed.

The entire point of the forum is not to run the city but to instead discuss the city, what the goals for the city should be, and make recommendations on how to achieve those goals.

The reason I don't want a traditional city council is twofold. First, I want to experiment with other forms of democracy; cities can be test grounds for ideas the same way regions are test grounds in larger nations. Second, and I will be very blunt here, I don't like letting a council decide production order and being required to follow it. It feels too much like I am ignoring my judgment in favor of the judgment of a crowd.

The forum, I believe, offers a good compromise between the unilateral decision-making present in most cities and what best seems to be the organized chaos of a city council. The forum allows for large input in times where it is needed and next to no input when the city is running smoothly. It allows for people to discuss the direction of the city and what they believe the goals should be, without getting too bogged down in the business of running the city. The initiative started because I was speaking to a group that really wanted to promote growth in the community.

I think that's a great idea. I just want someone or a group of people to be in charge of it. The complicated process is so that we don't end up with multiple organizations controlling advertisement.

The concern I had was that if one organization primarily controlled advertising, they could use it as a recruitment tool, which is not something I want.

So I worked with a colleague to make edits to the document. Take a look at it.

The idea was something I came up with while discussing it with a friend one night; basically, we need some form of organized advertising to bring in new members and keep the community healthy. My friend wanted to just appoint a cabinet position, but I felt it should be more independent from the actual government. So naturally, I added government regulation to create a semi-autonomous group that, given the appointment process, would presumably consist of reasonably well-driven individuals who are good at distancing themselves from politics.

It's also worth noting this is not a violation of dual mandate if someone holds this position, I believe. So in theory, the leader could appoint various individuals, and that would be completely fine.
